term: God (the God of classical theism; Lean `IsGod`)
definition: The case signature's `IsGod g`: g is God in the sense of the God of classical theism, not merely what is called God. The stages after stage 1 and the root use this predicate. Its content is fixed only by the open premises that use it: STMT-GOD-HAS-CLASSICAL-DIVINE-ATTRIBUTES (simple, perfect, good, infinite, immutable, eternal, one, with intellect and will) and, on the older stage-1 routes, the identification premise STMT-UNIQUE-PURE-ACT-FIRST-MOVER-IS-GOD. On the designated route it is also fixed by the fuller nominal premise STMT-GOD-NAMES-THE-FULLY-DESCRIBED-PRINCIPLE, which applies the proper name 'God' to `IsGod` directly (DISAMB-GOD). The individual attribute senses and their one-way mapping to the skeleton field are recorded in DEF-CLASSICAL-ATTRIBUTES-BUNDLE and linked from STMT-GOD-HAS-CLASSICAL-DIVINE-ATTRIBUTES.
note: Case vocabulary (TruthCore/Case/Catholicism/Root.lean), not a new proof that anything satisfies it. Dei Filius ch. 1 supplies the attribute list; the open bridge and its parameter mapping are explicit in DEF-CLASSICAL-ATTRIBUTES-BUNDLE. The linked sourced term definitions do not make the primitive IsGod or HasClassicalAttributes fields definitionally equivalent to their natural-language descriptions.
